Matt S: Heads-up: SeCureNet signed the POC. They're asking for BYO customer-managed keys via an HSM, automated rotation (30d preferred), and an encrypted key-escrow option with split custody. Need rough ops timeline, delta pricing for BYO-HSM + dedicated proxy, and what to put in the security questionnaire.
Julia L: Congrats. Quick plan: 1) Confirm vendor (AWS CloudHSM vs Thales Luna/Safenet) because proxy config changes. 2) Network & IAM allowlist doc + peering. 3) Customer supplies a wrapped test key and attestation artifact. 4) We deploy proxy in their VPC (or they host image in their registry) and run smoke tests. 5) Key ceremony / escrow steps.
Matt S: Can you rough out costs? Sales needs a ballpark today.
Julia L: Ballpark numbers: BYO-HSM support + dedicated proxy setup = one-time ~$9.5k. Dedicated reserved capacity for throughput ~ $1.5k/mo. If they want on-site facilitation for key ceremony or attestation validation, PS day rate ~$2k/day. If they require daily rotation (<24h) or multi-region mirrored HSMs, add infra premium.
Samir R: For the questionnaire we should draft answers for: HSM attestation formats we accept (CloudHSM certificates, Thales attestation blobs), audit log fields (key_id, operation, timestamp, requestor, request IP, attestation_token), retention options, split-escrow support, and exportability policy. Also call out we never store unwrapped customer key material.
Matt S: They asked: "Can we roll keys automatically and still keep previous ciphertexts for rollback?"
Julia L: Yes. We support scheduled rotation that triggers a rewrap operation. Old ciphertexts remain usable as long as the key version exists; we keep key-version metadata and envelope keys but not plaintext. If they want indefinite retention of ciphertext + metadata that's an add-on.
Priya N: Ops timeline estimate: once we have network allowlist, IAM role ARN, and a wrapped test key + vendor attestation, proxy deploy in their VPC can be done in ~2 business days (build + config), smoke tests 1 day, and a remote key ceremony + escrow validation 1-6 business days depending on their custodian availability. Full POC (end-to-end) normally ~5 business days after materials arrive.
Samir R: Caveat for CloudHSM: their cluster must be reachable from our proxy subnet; for Luna it's more certificate-heavy. We'll need vendor-specific runbook entries in the questionnaire. Also note: FIPS/HSM module version info should be captured for compliance buyers.
Matt S: What audit/log artifacts do we give them for compliance? They want per-request traceability.
Samir R: We emit an audit event for each operation with: key_id, key_version, operation (encrypt/decrypt/sign), timestamp, requestor identity (token or IAM principal), request_id, outcome, and HSM attestation digest when available. Logs are stored in their log sink if they want (recommended) and we can also retain copies per contract. No secret material is logged.
Julia L: I'll draft a short appendix for the SOW: responsibilities (customer provides wrapped test key, vendor attestation, network peering; Redwood provides proxy image, smoke tests, and a sample escrow manifest), success criteria (able to encrypt/decrypt using wrapped key end-to-end, attestation verified), and acceptance window.
Matt S: They mentioned split-escrow with two custodians. Any legal caveats?
Samir R: Legal usually wants: who controls the escrow keys, how access is granted, and what triggers retrieval. We'll note: Redwood can hold an encrypted escrow object but cannot unseal without the custodians per their split policy. We should mention customer-supplied escrow policies in the questionnaire answer.
Priya N: Deployment note: For air-gapped customers we can provide a container image and offline instructions; they must host the proxy in their subnet and provide instance to reach HSM. If they want us to run proxy in our infra with TLS to their HSM, that's more complexity and typically not allowed.
Matt S: Ops-bot created the workspace?
ops-bot: New POC workspace created: workspace/securenet-byok-2812345678 (assigned to @Julia L).
Matt S: Action items: Julia - put pricing line items + draft SOW into the workspace and ping legal; Samir - seed security questionnaire responses and include attestation/escrow wording; Priya - ops runbook checklist (network, IAM role, wrapped test key format, smoke tests). I'll ask the customer to confirm HSM vendor and produce a wrapped test key today.
Julia L: On it. I'll include a sample wrapped-key format (RSA-OAEP / AES-GCM envelope example) and a template attestation acceptance checklist.
Samir R: I'll flag multi-region HSM replication as an additional cost/risk item. If they require <24h rotation, call it out early.
Priya N: Noted re: registry options. We'll offer to push image to their ECR as part of setup if they provide repo access; otherwise we instruct them to pull from our signed image.
Matt S: Great. I'll update the customer and loop back. If they confirm Luna instead of CloudHSM, we'll need 1 extra day for config changes. Closing thread for now.
